  Public Works Commission/  1.A.
  Public Safety Commission
  Agenda Report
To:  Members of the Public Works Commission and Public Safety
  Commission

Prepared by:  Rob DuBoux, Public Works Director/City Engineer

Approved by:  Steve McClary, City Manager

Date prepared:  May 20, 2024  Meeting date: June 5, 2024

Subject:  Los Angeles County Measure R and Measure M Transportation
  Funding Projects

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Receive an update on Pacific Coast Highway Safety projects
on PCH funded using Los Angeles County Measure R and Measure M transportation
funds.

DISCUSSION: Los Angeles County Measure R and Measure M provide the City with a
funding source for transportation-related projects, programs, and improvements. The City
utilizes these funds for capital improvement projects and specifically PCH safety related
projects.

Measure R
Los Angeles County Measure R was approved by voters in 2008. This measure added a
half-cent sales tax for a period of thirty years to fund transportation projects and
improvements. Measure R is estimated to generate approximately $40 billion dollars
countywide. The following is a ·status of current PCH safety related projects funded by
Los Angeles County Measure R.

PCH Intersection Improvements at Trancas Canyon Road
Scope of Work:
This project includes installing a new west bound right turn lane at PCH and Trancas
Canyon Road. The proposed right turn lane will tie into the existing Caltrans Trancas
Bridge Replacement project and will include a right turn lane to enter the Trancas Country
Market.

  Page 1 of 3
  Agenda Item # 1.A.
 Status:
The project is in the 95% design stage. The project will be resubmitted to Caltrans for a
final review within the next 4 months. The construction of this project will not start until the
completion of the Caltrans Trancas Bridge Replacement Project. The bridge replacement
project is anticipated to be completed in the Spring 2025.

PCH Median Improvements: John Tyler Road to Puerco Canyon Road
Scope of Work:
This project includes improvements to the existing raised medians on PCH from John Tyler
Road to Puerco Canyon Road. The proposed new improvements include replacing the
existing center median material with new colored stamped concrete.
Status:
This project is wrapping up construction and is anticipated to be completed by the end of
June 2024.

PCH at Las Flores Cyn and Rambla Pacifico Intersection Improvements
Scope of Work:
This project includes modifying these intersections to improve overall safety on PCH. This
intersection has the most accidents of any intersection within the City. The project will
collaborate with Caltrans and develop a total redesign of the intersection to improve safety
and efficiency.
Status:
The project funding agreement is currently being reviewed by Metro. As soon as they
complete their review, a funding agreement will be sent to the City for Council approval.
Staff will be providing updates and will solicit feedback from the Commissions on this
project. Caltrans has several other projects within these intersections. The City will
coordinate this project with Caltrans’ improvement projects.

Measure M
Los Angeles County Measure M was approved by voters in 2016. This measure added an
additional half-cent sales tax beginning in 2017, which then increases to one percent on
July 1, 2039, immediately upon the expiration of the half-cent sales tax of Measure R.
Measure M does not have a sunset date. The following is a status of approved projects
funded with Los Angeles County Measure M.

PCH Crosswalk Improvements at Big Rock Drive and 20326 PCH
Scope of Work:
This project includes the installation of flashing warning beacons, raised medians, and a
pedestrian refuge area adjacent to 20326 PCH. Additionally, a new overhead flashing
"signal ahead" beacon will be placed 400 feet east of the Big Rock Drive intersection.
These enhancements were prioritized based on the 2015 PCH Safety Study.
Status:
The project funding agreement was approved by City Council on May 28, 2024. Staff will
prepare a Request for Qualifications for design professionals and will begin the design
process.
  Page 2 of 3
  Agenda Item # 1.A.
 PCH Median Improvements: Paradise Cove and Zuma Beach
Scope of Work:
This project consists of constructing a raised median within 500 feet at the intersections
of PCH and Paradise Cove Road in both directions (east and west) wherever a double-
yellow line exists and extend the northbound left-turn lane by 100 feet. The project will
also construct a new raised median approximately 500’ in length at PCH and Busch Drive
(east of Busch Drive) where the existing double yellow line exists.
Status:
The project funding agreement was approved by City Council on July 10, 2023. Staff has
received proposals from 2 design professionals. Staff has begun the process of evaluating
the proposals and will start the design process.

Pedestrian Undercrossing at Malibu Seafood
Scope of Work:
This project consists of constructing a new pedestrian undercrossing that would connect
Corral Beach, across from Malibu Seafood to the Sara Wan trailhead located next to
Malibu Seafood.
Status:
The project funding agreement was approved by City Council on February 26, 2024. Staff
has received one proposal and has begun the process of evaluating. The project design
will start immediately after the selection of the design consultant.

To:  Members of the Public Works Commission and Public Safety

Prepared by:  Rob DuBoux, Public Works Director/City Engineer

Approved by:  Steve McClary, City Manager

Date prepared:  May 20, 2024  Meeting date: June 5, 2024

Subject:  PCH Signal Synchronization System Improvements Project Update

RECOMMENDED ACTION: 1) Receive an update on the PCH Signal Synchronization
System Improvements project; and 2) Provide comments on the proposed safety
“enhancements.”

DISCUSSION: The PCH Signal Synchronization System Improvements Project is a
transportation project that was identified in the 2015 PCH Safety Study. The objective of
the project is to enhance and improve traffic signals throughout the Malibu PCH corridor,
which will reduce overall traffic congestion, improve traffic flow, and improve safety for all
modes of travel.

The project will install communication wiring between the existing traffic signals on PCH,
from Topanga Canyon Road to John Tyler Drive to allow the signals to communicate and
coordinate traffic signal timing. Vehicles traveling at the posted speed limits will likely
experience more green traffic lights. While those vehicles traveling faster than the posted
speed limit may experience more red traffic lights. This type of signal timing has been
demonstrated to lower overall speeds within a roadway while maintaining traffic flow.

The project will also utilize video cameras and other traffic detecting technology to gather
real-time traffic data. A new computerized traffic signal timing software system will receive
the real-time traffic data and can adjust the traffic signals based upon this real-time traffic
data. The new traffic signals will also be connected to the Caltrans Traffic Management
Center, allowing Caltrans to control and operate the signals and the signal system
remotely. These new traffic signal improvements will help alleviate traffic congestion on

  Page 1 of 2
  Agenda Item # 1.B.
 PCH and reduce the response time for Caltrans to manually adjust the traffic signal
timing. The new signal controllers and software can be used during emergency
evacuations.

The City’s contractor continues to work installing the underground communication conduit
and fiber optic line. The contractor is currently working north of Carbon Canyon Road near
the La Costa Pedestrian Crosswalk. They have installed approximately 30,000 linear feet
of conduit and fiber optic line. The contractor continues to make great progress on this
project and is currently on schedule to complete this project during the Spring of 2025.

Staff is currently evaluating additional improvements to this project which will increase the
traffic safety elements to this project and to PCH. The following items are currently being
evaluated for this project:

  1. Red-Light Enforcement Cameras – Staff is evaluating the installation of red-light
  enforcement cameras at five intersections between PCH and Malibu Canyon Road
  to Las Flores Canyon Road. These potential red-light enforcement cameras will be
  located at intersections that have a history of red-light infractions and accidents.
  Well-implemented red-light enforcement cameras can significantly improve
  intersection safety by modifying driver behavior and reducing dangerous red-light
  running.
  2. New Pedestrian Crosswalk and Traffic Signal – A new pedestrian crosswalk and
  traffic signal, located approximately 3,000 feet west of PCH and Carbon Canyon
  Road, is being evaluated. This crosswalk will be located adjacent to an existing
  beach access point and will allow pedestrians to safety cross PCH. The proposed
  new pedestrian signal will also provide an additional traffic break on PCH west of
  Carbon Canyon Road. The additional traffic break will allow the new signal timing
  system to control the traffic and speed in the area.
  3. New Signal Lights – The existing hybrid beacon pedestrian signal lighting at the
  La Costa Pedestrian Crosswalk will be exchanged with traditional pedestrian traffic
  signal lights. The proposed improvements will provide better visibility for vehicles
  and pedestrians at this existing intersection. This change will also allow this
  pedestrian signal to connect to the computerized traffic signal timing system.
  4. Traffic Safety Adaption System – This proposed system will utilize traffic radar
  cameras and traffic loops to evaluate traffic speeds on PCH. If the traffic speeds
  exceed the posted speed limit, the Traffic Safety Adaption System will trigger the
  upcoming traffic signals to turn to red and force traffic to slow down and stop.
  Additional signage will be utilized to warn vehicles about this system.

Staff is seeking comments from the Public Works Commission and Public Safety
Commission regarding these proposed “enhancements.”
